summary: Full backend + frontend testing of the new HARD email verification flow. All 10 pytest cases (register no-token, unverified login 403, verify token invalid/valid/reuse/expired, resend cooldown/verified/non-existent, admin grandfathering) and all 5 Playwright UI steps (register→pending-card, unverified login→pending-card, /verify-email?token=valid→success, /verify-email?token=invalid→error, post-verify login→onboarding) passed.
critical_code_review_comments: email_verify.py stores tokens plaintext; acceptable per spec (32-byte urlsafe random, single-use, 24h). Fine for now but consider hashing tokens at rest for defense-in-depth if DB read access ever leaks.

resend-verification rate-limit is per most-recent sent_at in the same collection — this correctly covers the register→resend sequence (register inserts a doc with sent_at). Confirmed via test (register then immediate resend returns 429). Good.
auth.py login sends welcome email lazily on first verified login and marks welcome_email_sent — solid pattern. No issue.
/api/auth/verify-email is a GET without CSRF concerns since it just consumes a random token; correct semantics.

Frontend AuthPage backToForm() only clears pendingEmail but preserves current mode; if the user reached pendingEmail via register, clicking 'Zurück zum Login' still leaves them on register-mode form. Minor UX polish — could auto-switch to login mode on back.
test_credentials: Admin sazhco0385@gmail.com / Bellakiki1 (grandfathered login verified). Ephemeral test users created with TEST_/test_ prefix + timestamp+uuid suffix, cleaned up after each run.
seed_data_creation: None persistent. Tests create fresh users per run and delete users + email_verifications + email_log after.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable regression test at /app/backend/tests/test_email_verification.py; runs in ~5s. Uses pymongo directly against MONGO_URL for token retrieval + expired-token seeding. Frontend test uses mongosh subprocess since Playwright container lacks pymongo.
